newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: Central American Parliament gets new deputies.
newsitem.headline: Central American Parliament gets new deputies.

text.p: The Central American Parliament must go beyond recommendations and build the legal basis for regional integration, the body's new president said during an inauguration of new deputies Monday.

"It is urgent to establish a framework containing the legal norms to regulate the orderly function of the pieces of integration," said Ernesto Lima Mena, the Salvadoran who will serve as president of the parliament for one year.
Sixty deputies from El Salvador, Guatemala and Honduras became official members of the Central American Parliament during the ceremony in Guatemala's capital. Each deputy serves for five years.
Lima Mena applauded the addition of twenty deputies from Nicaragua, who will join the three founding countries in the parliament in January.

"With this legitimate representation of most Central Americans, this parliament is prepared to take on greater responsibilities and will be able to make decisions in the formulation of policies for the process of integration," said Lima.

The new president said in its second five-year period the parliament will work more closely with the legislatures and political parties in each Central American country, to build the integration process.
Lima also said the Congress will establish stronger ties with the European Union, the Latin American Parliament and the Andean Parliament.
The Central American Parliament, formed in 1991, is a regional body for planning, research and integration. The presidency has rotated so far between El Salvador, Honduras and Guatemala.
Panama also has 20 seats in the parliament, but they are not full voting positions.
The Costa Rican Congress never ratified the international declaration that formed the Parliament and has no deputies seated in the body.
